question.text: In the futures market, initial margin is collected to:

answer.text: Cover the estimated risk to an open position over a 2-day horizon
Pay for the full value of the underlying asset upfront
Cover the brokerage charges of the trading member
Act as a deposit for the exchange membership fee

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 209, initial margin is collected using a formula that estimates the risk to an open position over a 2-day horizon. Exposure margin is collected separately as a percentage of notional value, and non-payment attracts penalties. The Trap: Margins are not the full contract value; they are not brokerage charges; and they are not a deposit for an exchange membership fee. Each of these distractors fails the source description on page 209. Note: Initial margin is a risk-management charge sized to a 2-day risk horizon; it is distinct from exposure margin, which is computed as a percentage of notional value.
